learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the true meaning of work, explore traditional Indian occupations, recognize gender issues in the workplace, and learn how to plan a meaningful career!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Work is primarily an activity done to produce, accomplish, or earn something. A livelihood refers to the means of making a living. A career encompasses a lifelong journey of building skills and growing in a chosen profession.

India is rich in traditional crafts like agriculture, weaving, pottery, and metalwork. These occupations are passed down through generations but are currently facing challenges from modern industrialization.
Gender roles have historically dictated types of work, but modern society is shifting towards equality. Women still face the 'double burden' of managing both professional work and household chores.
Ergonomics is the science of designing the workplace to fit the worker. Good ergonomics increases productivity and reduces physical strain and occupational hazards.
An entrepreneur is someone who starts a new business, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit. Key traits include innovation, hard work, and risk-taking.

fun_activity.title: 🕵️ Ergonomics Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Look at the chair and desk where you study. Are your feet flat on the floor? Is your screen at eye level? Adjust your study space to be 'ergonomically correct' and notice how your back feels after an hour!

exam_tips: 📌 Be ready to define 'Ergonomics' and explain its two main benefits: increased efficiency and reduced risk of injury.
📌 Clearly differentiate between 'Job' (done just for money) and 'Career' (a long-term professional journey with growth).
📌 Mention the 'double burden' when writing about women in the workforce.
quick_recap: ⭐ Work provides income, a sense of identity, and helps in contributing to society.
⭐ Traditional arts like Warli painting and Kanjeevaram sarees are essential parts of India's occupational heritage.
⭐ A healthy work environment must prioritize safety, fair wages, and ergonomic design.
